scope: General evidence for declared ingredient identities. Not product-specific exposure testing or personal diet clearance.
review_status: Source-backed educational draft; qualified clinical review pending.

profiles.function: Provides the drink's liquid base.
profiles.body_effect: Water contributes to fluid intake and normal hydration.
profiles.intake_context: Other ingredients still matter; water being the first ingredient does not make a sugary or caffeinated drink equivalent to plain water.

profiles.function: Dissolved carbon dioxide creates bubbles.
profiles.body_effect: Fizzy drinks can contribute to gas symptoms in some people; carbonation is not a sugar source.
profiles.intake_context: Plain carbonation and an acidic, sweetened soda are not interchangeable. Tolerance varies.

profiles.pattern: high fructose corn syrup|cane sugar|^sugar\b|^sucrose\b|\bdextrose\b|^glucose\b|^fructose\b|\bhoney\b|cassava root syrup
profiles.function: Adds sweetness and carbohydrate energy.
profiles.body_effect: Digestible carbohydrate can raise blood glucose. Frequent sugary-drink intake is associated with weight gain, type 2 diabetes and tooth decay.
profiles.intake_context: Use total and added sugar grams per serving. These associations do not mean one drink causes disease or that all sugar sources act identically in every person.

profiles.function: Contributes flavor and potentially sugars and nutrients.
profiles.body_effect: Juice can contribute naturally occurring sugars and carbohydrate energy, even when added sugar is zero.
profiles.intake_context: Use the actual total/added sugar panel. A concentrate's name does not establish its dose or mean that all its sugar is added sugar.

profiles.function: Provides strong sweetness using a small amount.
profiles.body_effect: Supplies phenylalanine: people with PKU need to avoid or restrict it. FDA supports its approved use conditions for the general population.
profiles.intake_context: A personal exposure cannot be calculated without its amount. Authorization is not permission for unlimited intake.

profiles.pattern: sucralose|acesulfame|steviol|stevia extract|stevia sweetener|stevia leaf extract|monk fruit
profiles.function: Adds sweetness with few or no calories at typical use amounts.
profiles.body_effect: These sugar substitutes generally do not raise blood glucose as sugar does. That is not proof of zero insulin response or weight-loss benefit from this drink.
profiles.intake_context: Exact dose and preparation matter. High-purity steviol glycosides are distinct from whole-leaf/crude stevia; do not infer the preparation from a vague label.

profiles.function: Sweetens with less energy than traditional sugar.
profiles.body_effect: Allulose is a sugar, not a sugar alcohol, but is metabolized differently. FDA allows it to be excluded from declared total/added sugar while remaining in total carbohydrate.
profiles.intake_context: Zero reported sugar is not a guarantee of zero calories or no individual metabolic response. The quantity still matters.

profiles.function: Provides sweetness; sugar alcohols are not drinking alcohol.
profiles.body_effect: Sugar-alcohol-containing products can contribute to gas symptoms in some people.
profiles.intake_context: Dose and tolerance matter. This name alone does not establish a measured disease risk or a safe number of cans.

profiles.function: Adds caffeine, whether isolated or supplied by a named extract.
profiles.body_effect: Can increase alertness, but may disrupt sleep or cause jitters, anxiety and a faster heartbeat.
profiles.intake_context: Count all caffeine sources. FDA's 400 mg/day context for most adults is not a target or a universal limit; sensitivity, pregnancy and medicines matter.

profiles.function: Provides brewed flavor and can naturally supply caffeine.
profiles.body_effect: Inherent caffeine may increase alertness and disturb sleep. Decaffeinated coffee is not necessarily caffeine-free.
profiles.intake_context: A coffee ingredient does not disclose caffeine mg. Do not assign a dose from another flavor, roast or bottle size.

profiles.function: A botanical source that can contribute caffeine.
profiles.body_effect: Its caffeine contributes to stimulant exposure; a botanical origin does not remove caffeine-related effects.
profiles.intake_context: Use a disclosed total caffeine amount, not an assumed extract-to-caffeine conversion.

profiles.function: Adds taste and aroma. Natural/artificial describes the source category, not a nutritional benefit.
profiles.body_effect: This is a grouped declaration, not an identified molecule. No specific bodily effect can be assigned to its undisclosed individual compounds.
profiles.intake_context: Natural origin is not a safety guarantee. Exact manufacturer disclosures can add detail, but general web recipes cannot identify this drink's blend.
profiles.disclosure: US labeling permits collective flavor names. The exact chemicals and doses are not disclosed by that phrase.

profiles.function: Adds tartness or controls acidity.
profiles.body_effect: Frequent acidic-drink contact can erode tooth enamel, including with sugar-free drinks.
profiles.intake_context: Frequency and contact time matter. An acid name does not measure this drink's pH or predict a personal erosion risk. Citric acid is not vitamin C.

profiles.pattern: sodium benzoate|potassium benzoate|benzoic acid|potassium sorbate|sorbic acid|sorbic and benzoic acids
profiles.function: Helps suppress microbial spoilage and maintain shelf life.
profiles.body_effect: The intended effect is on spoilage organisms in the drink, not a nutritional benefit in your body. Its presence alone is not evidence of toxicity.
profiles.intake_context: Concentration and conditions of use determine exposure. Do not treat benzoate as benzene or infer a contaminant from an ingredient list.

profiles.function: Changes appearance rather than demonstrating nutritional value.
profiles.body_effect: A color name alone cannot establish a specific bodily effect or a harmful dose in this drink.
profiles.intake_context: Authorization is substance/use-specific and can change. Neither natural nor artificial color is a blanket safety verdict; exposure and individual sensitivity matter.

profiles.function: May provide taste, electrolyte ions or acidity control, depending on the salt.
profiles.body_effect: Sodium supports fluid balance and nerve/muscle function. High total dietary sodium can raise blood pressure.
profiles.intake_context: Use disclosed sodium mg, including contributions from all ingredients. The 2,300 mg labeling DV is a comparison reference, not a personalized allowance.

profiles.pattern: potassium chloride|potassium citrate|potassium phosphate|mono-potassium phosphate|monopotassium phosphate|dipotassium phosphate
profiles.function: Can supply potassium ions and help regulate taste or acidity.
profiles.body_effect: Potassium is involved in nerve transmission and muscle/heart function. Kidney disease and some medicines can make excessive blood potassium a concern.
profiles.intake_context: The ingredient name does not quantify potassium. Do not infer an electrolyte benefit from potassium benzoate or acesulfame potassium.

profiles.function: May fortify the drink or help protect freshness.
profiles.body_effect: Vitamin C supports collagen formation, normal immune function and iron absorption.
profiles.intake_context: The name does not disclose the vitamin dose or show that this drink prevents illness. Large supplemental intakes can cause digestive symptoms; do not assume a beverage reaches those doses.

profiles.function: Adds a vitamin nutrient.
profiles.body_effect: B12 supports normal blood and nervous-system functions. Extra B12 does not improve energy or performance when intake is already adequate.
profiles.intake_context: Assess the actual vitamin amount and total intake. Its presence does not cancel caffeine effects or make an energy drink beneficial.

profiles.function: Adds a vitamin nutrient.
profiles.body_effect: B6 supports normal nutrient metabolism. Long-term high supplemental doses can damage nerves.
profiles.intake_context: That high-dose caution is not proof this drink causes nerve damage. Use a disclosed vitamin amount before assessing exposure.

profiles.function: Adds niacin or a named form such as niacinamide.
profiles.body_effect: B3 supports energy metabolism and cell function. Different forms have different high-dose adverse-effect profiles.
profiles.intake_context: Do not apply nicotinic-acid flushing warnings to niacinamide. A vitamin name does not disclose dose or establish extra energy from the drink.

profiles.function: An ingredient in some energy-drink mixtures.
profiles.body_effect: Taurine participates in normal processes including bile-acid-related fat digestion. That role does not demonstrate a benefit from drinking this product.
profiles.intake_context: Mixture effects, dose and evidence matter. Animal/basic research does not prove a beverage improves digestion, performance or disease resistance.

profiles.function: Can contribute protein, fat and naturally occurring lactose.
profiles.body_effect: Milk proteins are allergens. Lactose intolerance is different: poorly digested lactose can cause gas, bloating, pain or diarrhea.
profiles.intake_context: Use this drink's nutrient panel, not generic milk values. Lactose-free or lactase-treated milk still contains milk proteins.

profiles.function: May contribute protein or other formulation functions, depending on its form.
profiles.body_effect: Soy is a major food allergen; reactions can be serious in susceptible people.
profiles.intake_context: Ingredient screening is not a complete allergen/cross-contact assessment. Always check the package.

profiles.function: Provides a plant-based drink base.
profiles.body_effect: Its nutrient profile can differ substantially from dairy milk; a plant-based name does not establish its protein, sugar or vitamin amounts.
profiles.intake_context: Use the panel. Oats alone do not establish gluten-free status or freedom from milk/soy cross-contact.

profiles.function: Breaks lactose into simpler sugars.
profiles.body_effect: Lactase can reduce lactose-related digestive symptoms by helping break down lactose, but does not remove milk proteins.
profiles.intake_context: Its presence does not certify the finished drink is lactose-free or suitable for milk allergy.

profiles.pattern: inulin|chicory root fiber|cassava root fiber|acacia fiber|guar fiber|citrus fiber
profiles.function: Adds non-digestible carbohydrate/fiber, with effects depending on the type.
profiles.body_effect: Larger fiber intakes can contribute to gas or bloating in some people.
profiles.intake_context: Use a disclosed fiber amount. A fiber ingredient or proprietary mixture does not establish a disease-treatment or gut-health benefit from the drink.

profiles.function: Helps maintain texture, suspension or a stable mixture rather than adding a therapeutic effect.
profiles.body_effect: A formulation function does not establish a bodily benefit or harm at this drink's undisclosed dose.
profiles.intake_context: These are different substances, not one chemical. A focused identity/exposure review is needed before making more specific biological claims.

profiles.function: Binds metal ions to help protect product quality, including flavor.
profiles.body_effect: Its presence in a food is not evidence of a therapeutic chelation or detox effect in the drinker.
profiles.intake_context: Use-specific limits and actual concentration matter. Do not treat it as calcium fortification or transfer medical chelation claims to a beverage additive.

profiles.function: Helps keep flavoring-oil emulsions stable.
profiles.body_effect: This formulation role is not a nutritional benefit or evidence of a harmful dose. It is not classified as a sugar source simply because its name contains sucrose.
profiles.intake_context: The regulatory manufacturing limit is not the measured concentration in this drink or a personal allowance.

profiles.function: Adjusts citrus-oil density to support the beverage formulation.
profiles.body_effect: This product-processing function does not establish a bodily benefit or harm at an undisclosed dose.
profiles.intake_context: Do not confuse this ingredient with glycerin or assign a sugar amount from its name.

profiles.function: Helps produce consistent texture and a stable drink.
profiles.body_effect: Its presence is not a measured fiber amount or evidence of a therapeutic gut benefit.
profiles.intake_context: Fermentation-derived manufacture does not mean the drink contains live probiotic organisms.

profiles.pattern: calcium carbonate|tricalcium phosphate|dicalcium phosphate|calcium fumarate|calcium lactate|calcium chloride|calcium chlorides
profiles.function: May provide mineral fortification or a formulation function.
profiles.body_effect: Calcium supports bones, teeth and normal muscle/nerve activity.
profiles.intake_context: The compound name does not disclose elemental calcium mg or establish a benefit from this drink. Calcium disodium EDTA is a different function, not calcium fortification.

profiles.pattern: magnesium sulfate|magnesium chloride|magnesium and calcium chlorides
profiles.function: May contribute minerals for taste or fortification.
profiles.body_effect: Magnesium participates in normal muscle/nerve function. Impaired kidney function can change handling of excessive mineral exposure.
profiles.intake_context: Use actual magnesium mg if disclosed. High-dose supplement/medicine findings should not be treated as effects of an ordinary beverage dose.

profiles.function: May supply mineral ions or regulate the formulation.
profiles.body_effect: Phosphorus participates in bones, cells and energy processes. Severe kidney disease can alter phosphorus handling.
profiles.intake_context: This name does not quantify phosphorus or establish that extra intake benefits the drinker.

profiles.function: Adds riboflavin as a nutrient.
profiles.body_effect: B2 supports normal cell function and conversion of food into usable energy.
profiles.intake_context: It is not a stimulant or evidence of an extra energy boost. Use the declared amount to assess intake.

profiles.function: May provide vitamin fortification; beta-carotene can also provide color.
profiles.body_effect: Vitamin A supports normal vision and immune function. Preformed vitamin A and provitamin carotenoids are not interchangeable for dosing.
profiles.intake_context: Form and amount matter. Do not transfer high-dose preformed-vitamin-A findings to every carotenoid color ingredient.

profiles.function: Adds a vitamin nutrient, including D2 or D3 when named.
profiles.body_effect: Vitamin D helps calcium absorption and supports normal bone function.
profiles.intake_context: Presence alone does not show this drink prevents disease or that more intake is better. Use a disclosed nutrient amount.

profiles.function: May fortify the drink or help protect freshness.
profiles.body_effect: Vitamin E has an antioxidant role in cells and supports normal immune function.
profiles.intake_context: Tocopherols in a formulation do not quantify vitamin nutrition. Do not assume high-dose supplement effects at ordinary beverage amounts.

profiles.function: Adds a named botanical to the formulation.
profiles.body_effect: Evidence on specific ginseng preparations does not establish an energy/performance benefit from this drink. Ginseng may affect sleep or interact with medicines.
profiles.intake_context: Species, preparation and dose matter; clinical studies are often small or short. Do not reconstruct a proprietary mixture from generic extract studies.

profiles.pattern: canola oil|low erucic acid rapeseed oil
profiles.function: Adds an edible oil to the drink's formulation.
profiles.body_effect: Fat contributes food energy; the ingredient name alone does not establish a therapeutic benefit.
profiles.intake_context: Use this drink's fat and calorie panel, not assumed oil quantities or generic heart-health promises.

profiles.function: Used for aeration or dispensing, not nutrient fortification.
profiles.body_effect: This food-processing role is not a nutritional benefit or the same exposure as inhaling gas.
profiles.intake_context: Nitrogen (N2) and nitrous oxide (N2O) are different. A 'nitro' marketing name alone does not identify which gas is used.
